evidence.detail: rs/g/b is abstract and defines exactly two clock operations: reset via void a() and wait/advance via int a(int,int), returning the number of client cycles to process.
The base client rs/C stores this abstract type as its runtime clock and its exact factory be() constructs rs/g/d first, catching any Throwable and falling back to rs/g/c.
The base client main loop repeatedly calls ClientClock.a(cycleMillis, minimumSleep), uses the returned integer as the number of logic cycles to run, then renders once.

candidates.note: ClientClock is fixed by the abstract reset/wait-for-cycles contract and direct ownership by the base client main loop. Confidence is 0.999.

evidence.detail: rs/g/c extends the abstract client clock and uses System.currentTimeMillis through a synchronized monotonic-adjustment helper.

The clock keeps a ten-entry long timestamp ring, derives a bounded 25..256 cycle-rate accumulator and minimum sleep delay, shifts prior samples when sleeping, and returns the number of accumulated client cycles.
rs/C.be() instantiates this class only when construction of the nanosecond clock throws, making it the exact millisecond fallback implementation.
Its wait path delegates millisecond sleeping to rs/g/e before advancing the fixed-point cycle accumulator.

candidates.note: MillisClientClock is fixed by currentTimeMillis timing, ten-sample smoothing and exact fallback selection in rs/C.be(). Confidence is 0.999.

evidence.detail: rs/g/d extends the abstract client clock and initializes/resets its primary timestamp exclusively from System.nanoTime().
Its wait method computes target cycle duration in nanoseconds, sleeps against the next scheduled timestamp, advances by cycleMillis * 1,000,000 and caps catch-up cycles at 10.
rs/C.be() attempts to construct this implementation first and returns it directly; only a thrown Throwable causes the millisecond clock fallback.
The clock also contains a live-client branch using Launcher.n().o(), Client.au() and Client.cc while preserving the same nanosecond cycle scheduling responsibility.

candidates.note: NanoClientClock is fixed by System.nanoTime scheduling and exact primary selection in rs/C.be(). Confidence is 0.999.

evidence.detail: rs/g/e contains one public static long-millisecond sleep operation and no other runtime state or responsibility.
For positive delays divisible by 10, the helper sleeps delay-1 milliseconds and then 1 millisecond; otherwise it performs one Thread.sleep(delay), matching the timing clocks' shared sleep path.
Both rs/g/c and rs/g/d invoke this helper from their client-clock wait implementations; no unrelated exact-v308 consumer was found.

candidates.note: SleepUtil is descriptive exact-behavior recovery for the clock family's shared millisecond Thread.sleep wrapper. Confidence is 0.998.
